newsitem.title: UK: Utd Airlines set to slam BA /AA deal in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Utd Airlines set to slam BA /AA deal in U.S.

text.p: United Airlines, the U.S. transatlantic carrier, is set to warn later on Tuesday that the proposed alliance between British Airways Plc and AMR Corp's American Airlines represents "an unprecedented threat to global competition."

The warning is due to be made by Cyril Murphy, vice president of international affairs, in his testimony to the U.S. Senate sub-committee on anti-trust, business rights and competition, a statement issued by the airline in London said.

United Airlines said Murphy would tell the Senate committee "BA and American are the two biggest carriers at the most uncompetitive airport in Europe (Heathrow). Together these two carriers will dominate traffic..."
He went on to say that if American was given regulatory clearance to enter a further alliance with Japan Air Lines (JAL): "This would give BA, American and JAL a de facto lock on global competition."
